title: Boards of laws that name no relation
claim: Names are the reduced words of F2 = <x, y>; e(u, v) says names u and v are one place, under transitivity, letter closure e(u, v) -> e(ug, vg) and constancy e(u, v) -> s(u) = s(v); a law is finitely many clause templates over a finite alphabet, and it names no relation when every identity literal relates the same offset of two base names. Proved: (1) the board states are exactly the subgroups of F2 with their Schreier graphs, and on a ball B_L exactly the restrictions of right congruences (every one of finite index); (2) with no positive identity literal beyond the board axioms, refining an allowed board keeps it allowed, so the tree is allowed whenever any state is and allowed boards are closed under covering; (3) unfolding: if a law names no relation and allows an infinite board, it allows the tree, so no such law forces an infinite board; (4) every finite board is the only board of some law that names no relation; (5) two different boards differ in infinitely many identity distinctions and off the tree every place holds infinitely many names, so no distinction of a state off the tree, and no identity distinction anywhere, is flipped by a finite change; (6) for value laws the collapse is allowed iff a constant colouring is iff every board is; (7) identity of indiscernibles at radius r makes every board finite (at most q^|B_r| places), at radius 1 with one bit the boards are exactly the balanced view sets, and every plane-like abelian board there has a non-abelian sibling (at radius r, above q^(3^r - 1) places); (8) the commutator rule e(u, u x y X Y) with an aperiodic Wang-tile law forces exactly the plane.
failure_conditions: A law of ticket B's census with an allowed board whose listed cover is not allowed (target 2).
A law of the census allowing the collapse without allowing every listed board (target 6).
A law of the census with a plane-like abelian board under identity of indiscernibles at radius 1 and no non-abelian one (target 7).
A law that names no relation, with an allowed infinite board and no allowed state on the tree (target 3).
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of identity distinctions on the names of the free group on two letters; finitary laws over finite alphabets. Identity distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact: equality is not a binding (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's assignment on 2026-11-10 (backlog B92).

validation.novelty: Ingredients classical (Schreier graphs, Stallings foldings, compactness, aperiodic tilings); the unfolding theorem (3) and its reading as an obstruction for boards made of distinctions are new as far as found (bounded search, 2026-11-10, not a priority claim); folklore risk moderate for 1, 2, 6 and 8, low to moderate for 3, 5 and 7.
